$comment: x402 reference placement — the HTTP-LAYER CARRIER, cut against the live x402 v2 specification (x402-foundation/x402@db5da2e65952, specs/x402-specification-v2.md, read 2026-08-11). THIS IS NOT THE x402 WELD: @integraledger/lcp-binding-evm-x402 binds atrHash into the EIP-3009 nonce and answers 'what did the money commit to?'. This area answers a different question — 'where does the reference ride on the wire?' — and both are true at once. GATE (§7): the live spec confirms (a) `extensions` is carried on PaymentRequired, PaymentPayload AND SettlementResponse, (b) each entry carries `info` ('Extension-specific data provided by the server') and `schema` ('JSON Schema defining the expected structure of info'), (c) the echo rule — 'The client must include at least the info received; it may append additional info but cannot delete or overwrite existing info' — and (d) §6.1 reserves `assetTransferMethod` and `paymentFlow` inside PaymentRequirements.extra as protocol-governed names. (c) is why the top-level map is CANONICAL here: it is the carrier the protocol itself protects. (d) is half of why `place` now WRITES the extra mirror — the predecessor corpus pinned 'place never touches extra' on the ground that extra was wholly scheme-private, and §6.1 withdrew that ground; LCP v1.38 §C.4's own Tier A illustration carrying atrHash AND legalContextUrl there is the other half, because a reader built from the spec's example reads extra first. The written mirror merges around the scheme's own keys and never touches the reserved names. THE ADVERTISEMENT IS ONE ACT: the manifest declares two terms-URL slots (info-side, extra-side), place writes both and REQUIRES the URL of an integrity-bearing reference — a hash no counterparty can resolve is unverifiable by construction, which is the defect integra-protocol#8 measured: every published reader demanded the locator and no published writer placed it. extract reconciles the two slots, refusing disagreement, and reports absence as a typed value because pre-fix emissions are still evidence. THE ALIAS HAS A DIFFERENT ENCODING FROM THE CANONICAL FIELD, and x402 is the only protocol in the set where that is true: the canonical slot holds a §8.1-derived object, `accepts[0].extra.atrHash` holds a BARE hash. The alias is index 0 ONLY, matching what buyer parsers read. The extension KEY is `legalContext`, not a reverse-domain name: x402 imposes no namespace rule and `legalContext` is what sellers emit, what buyer parsers read, and what §C.4's own illustration shows. carrierTypes is sha256 ALONE — the url admission is WITHDRAWN, because the schema member this placement itself puts on the wire (the authority document's shape, drift-gated in conformance) is const sha256, so a url reference would emit a challenge violating its own adjacent schema. Case inputs are shaped {protocol, op, ref?, termsUrl?, doc} under `input` (the runner passes only c.input); refusal expecteds pin {refused, haltClass, code} and omit `detail`; success arms pin the WHOLE Outcome, in the exact key order the adapter emits, because the runner's deepEqual is JSON.stringify equality. The `roundtrip` op runs place then extract inside the subject and pins the recovered advertisement — the composition certification the predecessor corpus lacked.

manifest.specRef: x402 v2 (x402-foundation/x402@db5da2e65952 specs/x402-specification-v2.md, read 2026-08-11) — top-level extensions map carried on PaymentRequired/PaymentPayload/SettlementResponse, each entry {info, schema}; accepts[].extra carries the §C.4 mirror (reserved names per §6.1 untouched; gate discharged: see README)

cases.name: place writes the whole advertisement — wrapper, both terms-URL slots, and the §C.4 extra mirror
cases.$comment: The slot does not hold the reference directly — it holds {info, schema}, where `schema` is the INLINED carrier schema (equal to the authority document minus $id/$defs; the conformance drift gate holds that equality). `info` carries the locator beside the reference because the schema REQUIRES it, and the same pair lands in accepts[0].extra because LCP v1.38 §C.4's Tier A illustration is a reader some counterparty built. This one case pins the complete wire shape a third-party seller assembles — the composition integra-protocol#8 measured as impossible.

schema.title: legalContext — x402 extension info
schema.description: The `info` payload of the `legalContext` x402 extension at challenge time: a Legal Context Protocol reference to the terms governing this transaction, plus the URL the terms document can be fetched from. The reference identifies the exact terms document; it is not the terms. This describes a technology harness and asserts nothing about whether any agreement is lawful, sound or enforceable.

type.description: The digest algorithm over the terms document. `sha256` is the only value this version defines.

value.description: The atrHash — SHA-256 of the terms document, lowercase hex with an 0x prefix.

legalContextUrl.description: Where the terms document this hash covers can be fetched. A reader verifies the document against `value`; the URL is a locator and never the authority.

cases.name: a server-advertised sibling extension survives — clients MUST NOT delete or overwrite
cases.$comment: x402's own rule about x402's own map. A placement that pruned a sibling extension would make the client that used it non-conformant.

cases.name: the extra mirror MERGES into the scheme's own object — sibling keys are the scheme's and survive
cases.$comment: REVERSED from the predecessor corpus, which pinned 'place never touches the per-requirement extra'. Three grounds, recorded in the manifest docblock: §6.1 reserves names inside `extra`, so it is host-managed rather than wholly scheme-private; §C.4's Tier A illustration carries atrHash AND legalContextUrl there, so a reader built from the spec's example reads extra first; and the shipped buyer parser reconciles both carriers, refusing disagreement, so the mirror cannot drift silently. The scheme's own keys (name/version here — the live spec's example content) are merged around, never replaced, and the reserved names are untouched.

cases.name: place REFUSES a url carrier — the admission is WITHDRAWN, and the schema on the wire is why
cases.$comment: The predecessor permitted url and recorded in the same docblock that the permission was wider than any shipped reader — well-formed against the manifest, refused at every read. The withdrawal ground is structural: the `schema` member this placement puts on the wire is the authority document's shape, whose `type` is const sha256, so a url reference would emit a challenge that violates its own adjacent schema.

cases.name: place REFUSES a challenge whose extensions is a STRING — that map is ABOVE the field's direct holder
cases.$comment: The malformed-container rule, ratified in binding-core: `extensions` sits one level above `legalContext`, and replacing an intermediate discards everything beneath it.

cases.name: place REFUSES an ARRAY extensions map — the case where replacing it would DESTROY sibling entries
place REFUSES a NUMERIC extensions map — the branch a string and an array both leave open
place REFUSES a NULL extensions map — present-holding-null is not absent
an unmergeable OWN entry IS replaced — the other half of the same rule, at the direct holder
cases.$comment: `extensions.legalContext` is the direct holder of `.info`, so a present-but-unmergeable value THERE is replaced — and it costs the host nothing, because `legalContext` is our own extension key and the only thing dropped was never a conformant entry. The sibling `someOther` proves the replacement is scoped to our entry and not to the map.

cases.name: place REFUSES a null document — minting the challenge is not the extension point's job
place REFUSES an ARRAY document — a JSON array is not an x402 challenge
place REFUSES a NON-OBJECT document — a string is not a challenge with room in it
place REFUSES a challenge with NO payable requirement — the mirror slots live inside accepts[0]
cases.$comment: The writer only ever ENTERS an existing element — the host builds its own list, and index 0 on an empty accepts names an element the host never put there. A challenge nothing can pay is not a challenge this placement can advertise in, and refusing beats minting {"0":…} structure that reads as a list to every index-aware parser.

cases.name: place REFUSES a carrier type the manifest does not permit
place REFUSES a permitted type whose VALUE is not valid for it
place REFUSES a sha256 advertisement with NO terms URL — the composition defect, closed at the source
cases.$comment: integra-protocol#8's shape: the published buyer demands the locator (a hash no counterparty can resolve is unverifiable by construction), so an emitter that omits it mints a challenge nothing accepts. The refusal lands at the seller, where the missing datum is — not at the counterparty, where it surfaced.

cases.name: place REFUSES a cleartext terms URL — minting a challenge every buyer refuses is not a success path
place is pure — the input challenge is not mutated
cases.$comment: Purity is a property of the CALL, not of its result, and the URL writes descend through the host's own accepts element — the walk that would be easiest to get wrong in place.

cases.name: extract reads the canonical extensions slot, terms URL beside the reference
extract reads the long-standing shipped carrier, verbatim
cases.$comment: The document is exactly what a conformant seller emits — the pair in both carriers, `schema` beside `info` — and the reader answers it as ONE agreement: reference reconciled by strength order, URL reconciled across both declared slots. A reader that rejected our own shipped shape would be the defect.

schema.title: legalContext — x402 extension info
schema.description: The `info` payload of the `legalContext` x402 extension at challenge time: a Legal Context Protocol reference to the terms governing this transaction, plus the URL the terms document can be fetched from. The reference identifies the exact terms document; it is not the terms. This describes a technology harness and asserts nothing about whether any agreement is lawful, sound or enforceable.

type.description: The digest algorithm over the terms document. `sha256` is the only value this version defines.

value.description: The atrHash — SHA-256 of the terms document, lowercase hex with an 0x prefix.

legalContextUrl.description: Where the terms document this hash covers can be fetched. A reader verifies the document against `value`; the URL is a locator and never the authority.

cases.name: extract reads a pre-fix emission — reference present, no URL anywhere — as EVIDENCE, not a refusal
cases.$comment: Documents emitted before the write path existed are still on wires. The reference is evidence; whether to transact against a locator-less advertisement is the GATE's decision, made where the buyer's policy lives — the reader only says which absence this is (the seller left declared slots empty, as opposed to a protocol with no slot).

cases.name: extract also reads the per-requirement extra.atrHash alias — a BARE hash, not an lcp: string
a URL present in only ONE slot answers — one-present wins, agreement is only demanded of two
cases.$comment: §C.4's illustration carries the pair in extra alone, and a reader that demanded both slots would refuse the spec's own example.

cases.name: the bare alias accepts UPPERCASE hex and returns it unnormalized
cases.$comment: Hex is case-insensitive (the ATR-canon any-case rule), so a conformant counterparty advertising uppercase must not be false-negatived. Normalization belongs to the comparison — verify's referencePlacementStep canonicalizes both sides — not to the read.

cases.name: the canonical extensions slot wins when both reference carriers are present
cases.$comment: Strength order as data: the canonical field answers first even when the alias carries a different datum. A reader that took the alias would let whichever carrier a middlebox rewrote decide what the record cites. DISCLOSED DIVERGENCE from a strict buyer gate: such a reader may prefer accepts[].extra (the per-requirement carrier) and REFUSES outright when the two carriers disagree, where this area answers with the canonical slot and says nothing. A placement is structural and does not adjudicate the host's document; a buyer parser may. Both behaviours are designed, the divergence is recorded in the README, and that parser is where the two readers reconcile. (The TERMS-URL slots reconcile here — mismatch refuses — because both slots are this manifest's own declarations, not the host's carriers.)

cases.name: extract REFUSES two terms-URL slots that DISAGREE — a seller must not advertise different terms to different readers
cases.$comment: The write side puts one URL in both slots; a document carrying two different ones lets the seller disown whichever reading lost. Refused at the read, not resolved by preference.

cases.name: extract REFUSES a malformed terms-URL slot even when the other slot reads cleanly
cases.$comment: A half-corrupt advertisement is not resolved by preferring the clean half — https is the only scheme either side of the seam accepts.

cases.name: a canonical slot that is present but UNREADABLE is not abandoned for the alias
cases.$comment: The anti-substitution rule. An unknown carrier type in the canonical slot refuses; it does not silently fall through to the weaker carrier, which would let a counterparty that corrupted the protected map steer the read to the scheme's own object.

cases.name: extract REFUSES a decoded carrier type this field may not hold
extract REFUSES a url reference in the canonical slot — the withdrawn admission, read side
cases.$comment: The predecessor corpus ANSWERED this document with the url reference. Withdrawing the admission changes the read too, deliberately: a permission no shipped reader accepted was an ecosystem claim, and the schema this placement itself puts on the wire is const sha256.

cases.name: extract REFUSES a corrupt bare hash in the alias
extract refuses when neither carrier is present
an entry advertising `schema` but no `info` reads as ABSENT
cases.$comment: The declared field is the `.info` leaf, not the entry. A server that advertised the extension without data has carried no reference, and reading the entry itself as one would hand a caller {schema:{...}} to decode.

cases.name: an accepts value that is not an array reads as ABSENT — the kit's read-side convention
cases.$comment: Same ratified convention placement-acp established (metadata holding a number reads as absent): an unreadable container yields no reference on the READ side, and document-malformed is reserved for a non-object document.

cases.name: the alias is index 0 ONLY — a hash on the SECOND requirement is not read
cases.$comment: The declared locator is `accepts.0.extra.atrHash` and the manifest means it. Buyer parsers read accepts[0] for the same reason: the reference must bind to the requirement actually being paid, and 'search every requirement' would let a seller hide a second set of terms behind an alternative it never expects to be chosen.

cases.name: extract REFUSES a null document
ROUNDTRIP — a third party's whole path: assemble from the manifest, read with the kit, one agreement out
cases.$comment: The gap that let integra-protocol#8 ship: every place case certified the write and every extract case certified the read, and no case ever fed one to the other — the two halves were separately conformant and jointly broken. This op runs place then extract inside the subject and pins the recovered advertisement, so the corpus itself now fails if the written document stops being readable.
